1.description: Magpies conspicuous against snow, foraging in small groups and calling with harsh chattering
1.childFriendlyNote: A big black-and-white bird with a super long tail hops through the snow. Its feathers flash blue and green in the sun!

1.description: Mule deer gathered in lower valleys and foothills, browsing on sagebrush and dried grasses
1.childFriendlyNote: Deer with big ears like a mule stand together in the snowy fields, nibbling on whatever they can find

1.description: Fresh snow reveals tracks of cottontail rabbits, coyotes, and squirrels, perfect for reading stories left behind
1.childFriendlyNote: After fresh snow, look for little footprints: tiny bunny hops, dog-like coyote prints, and squirrel paw-pairs!

1.description: Red-tailed hawks perched on utility poles and bare cottonwoods, scanning for rodents in snow-covered fields
1.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk sits on a pole like a statue, then suddenly dives. It spotted a mouse hiding under the snow!

1.description: Ponderosa pines stand green against the snow; on sunny winter days press your nose to the bark for a butterscotch scent
1.childFriendlyNote: Find a big pine tree with orange-brown bark and sniff it on a sunny day. It smells like vanilla cookies!

1.description: Bold Steller's jays visiting feeders and picnic areas, dark blue with a tall black crest
1.childFriendlyNote: A dark blue bird with a spiky hairdo screams from a pine tree. Steller's jays are loud and bossy!

2.description: Magpies starting to gather sticks for their large domed nests, chattering in cottonwoods
2.childFriendlyNote: Magpies are already collecting sticks for their nests. They build giant stick domes as big as a beach ball!

2.description: Elk herds concentrated in valley bottoms and lower meadows, bulls have shed or are shedding antlers
2.childFriendlyNote: Huge elk stand together in snowy fields. Some boys have lost their antlers and look surprised without them!

2.description: Juncos hopping on snowy ground beneath feeders, flashing white outer tail feathers when they fly
2.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds with white bellies hop around in the snow. When they fly away, their tails flash bright white!

2.description: Cottontail rabbit tracks in snow, two big back feet in front of two small front feet in a bounding pattern
2.childFriendlyNote: Bunny tracks in the snow look backwards. The big back feet land in front of the little front feet!

2.description: Great horned owls hooting at dusk, already nesting. Listen for deep "hoo-hoo-hooooo hoo-hoo" duets
2.childFriendlyNote: At bedtime, listen for a deep "hoo-hoo-hooooo". That's a huge owl with ear tufts sitting on eggs in the cold!

3.description: Magpies actively building large stick nests in cottonwoods and willows, visible against bare branches
3.childFriendlyNote: Look up in bare trees for huge messy stick nests. Magpies are busy builders even in the freezing cold!

3.description: Mule deer in winter herds, bucks dropping antlers. Search sunny hillsides for shed antlers
3.childFriendlyNote: Deer are dropping their antlers like losing teeth. If you're lucky you might find one on the ground!

3.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring over open fields, their rusty-red tails glowing in winter sun
3.childFriendlyNote: A hawk circles high in the blue sky, screaming "keeee-arrr!". Look for the red tail catching the light

3.description: Ponderosa pines vivid green against grey sky, bark smelling of butterscotch in afternoon sun
3.childFriendlyNote: Press your nose into the jigsaw-puzzle bark of a ponderosa. Warm sunshine makes it smell like butterscotch!

3.description: Great horned owls incubating eggs, the female sitting tight through snowstorms on the nest
3.childFriendlyNote: Mama owl is sitting on her eggs in the freezing cold, covered in snow like a feathery blanket, so brave!

3.description: Coyote tracks in snow following a straight line, unlike dog tracks that wander. Listen for yipping at dawn
3.childFriendlyNote: Coyote paw prints march in a neat line through the snow. Dogs zigzag, but coyotes walk like they have somewhere to go!

4.description: Magpie nests growing larger, pairs defending territory with loud rattling calls
4.childFriendlyNote: Magpie couples guard their stick-castle nest and scream at anyone who walks too close!

4.description: Flocks of juncos foraging under feeders, scratching through snow for seeds
4.childFriendlyNote: Tiny grey birds scratch the snow with both feet at once, hop-scratch, hop-scratch, looking for seeds!

4.description: Elk bulls have dropped antlers; cows and calves huddled in valley meadows, pawing through snow for grass
4.childFriendlyNote: Big elk use their hooves like shovels to dig through the snow and find dry grass underneath!

4.description: Red-tails beginning courtship flights, pairs circling together and diving
4.childFriendlyNote: Two hawks dance in the sky together, swooping and spinning. They're showing off for each other!

4.description: Intricate hoarfrost on fence wires, grass blades, and tree branches in the cold dry mountain air
4.childFriendlyNote: Every blade of grass wears a sparkly ice coat. The dry mountain air makes the fanciest frost crystals!

5.description: Great horned owl chicks hatching, fluffy white owlets visible in nests if you know where to look
5.childFriendlyNote: Baby owls are hatching in the cold! They look like fluffy white cotton balls with big dark eyes

5.description: Magpies finishing their elaborate roofed nests, lining the inside with mud and soft materials
5.childFriendlyNote: Magpies put a roof on their nest! They carry mud in their beaks to make the inside smooth and cozy

5.description: Coyotes in mating season, pairs howling together at dawn and dusk. Yipping chorus carries far in cold air
5.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, coyotes sing together, yip yip yip awooooo! It sounds like a wild song bouncing off the mountains

5.description: Mule deer in winter survival mode, browsing sagebrush and juniper on south-facing slopes
5.childFriendlyNote: Deer choose sunny hillsides where snow melts first, clever trick to find something green to eat!

5.description: Steller's jays caching seeds and visiting feeders, their harsh "shack-shack-shack" calls echoing in pines
5.childFriendlyNote: This bossy blue bird buries seeds in secret hiding spots. It remembers thousands of hiding places!

6.description: Chickadees beginning spring song, a clear whistled "fee-bee" replacing winter "chick-a-dee-dee" calls
6.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee changes its song! Instead of "chick-a-dee," it now whistles "fee-bee". Spring is coming!

6.description: Red-tailed hawks performing spectacular courtship dives and talon-locking aerial displays
6.childFriendlyNote: Two hawks grab each other's feet high in the sky and tumble together: it's their way of saying "I love you!"

6.description: Owl chicks growing, parents hunting actively at dusk to feed hungry nestlings
6.childFriendlyNote: Parent owls fly silently in the dark, bringing mice and rabbits back to their hungry fluffy babies

6.description: Ponderosa pines fragrant on warm February afternoons, bark puzzle-pieces catching the low sun
6.childFriendlyNote: On a warm sunny afternoon, the ponderosa bark smells like a bakery: vanilla and butterscotch!

6.description: Junco flocks still abundant at feeders, some males beginning to sing a simple trill on mild days
6.childFriendlyNote: Little grey juncos start practising their spring song, a fast twinkling trill like a tiny bell!

7.description: Chickadees singing "fee-bee" spring song more frequently, pairs beginning to form
7.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees are pairing up! Two tiny birds chase each other through the branches whistling "fee-bee!"

7.description: First male red-winged blackbirds arriving at lower-elevation marshes, claiming territories early
7.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird with bright red shoulder patches puffs up and sings "conk-la-ree!" from a cattail

7.description: Elk still in winter herds but starting to shift upslope on warm days, bulls growing new antler nubs
7.childFriendlyNote: Bull elk have fuzzy little bumps on their heads, brand new antlers starting to sprout like magic!

7.description: Early robins appearing in lower elevations, running across lawns on warm days
7.childFriendlyNote: The first robin of spring! Watch it run, stop, tilt its head, then pull a worm. It's listening for lunch!

7.description: Mated coyote pairs seeking den sites, tracks in snow often showing two animals side by side
7.childFriendlyNote: Two sets of coyote tracks walk side by side in the snow: a coyote couple looking for a home for their babies!

8.description: Prairie dogs beginning to emerge from burrows on warm afternoons, sitting at burrow entrances
8.childFriendlyNote: Chubby little prairie dogs poke their heads out of their holes on sunny days and bark like tiny dogs!

8.description: Pussy willow buds swelling along streams and ditches, soft silvery catkins emerging from dark buds
8.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy silver puffs pop out of the willow branches. Touch one gently, it feels like a tiny kitten's paw!

8.description: More red-winged blackbirds arriving, males perching prominently and singing from cattails and fences
8.childFriendlyNote: Red-winged blackbirds flash their red and yellow shoulder patches like badges: "This marsh is mine!"

8.description: Robins increasing in numbers, singing at dawn from rooftops and bare trees
8.childFriendlyNote: Robins sing "cheerily, cheer-up, cheerio!" from the highest branches. They're the morning alarm clock!

8.description: Chickadee pairs investigating tree cavities and nest boxes, singing "fee-bee" constantly
8.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees peek into every hole in every tree. They're house-hunting for the perfect spot to raise babies!

9.description: Early crocuses pushing through snow in town gardens and south-facing beds, purple and yellow blooms
9.childFriendlyNote: Brave little purple and yellow flowers push right through the snow. They can't wait for spring!

9.description: Prairie dogs more active on warm days, standing upright on mounds and giving alarm barks
9.childFriendlyNote: Prairie dogs stand straight up like little soldiers and bark when they see something scary, even you!

9.description: Red-winged blackbird males in full territorial display, singing and flaring red epaulets
9.childFriendlyNote: The blackbird puffs up like a balloon and flashes its red shoulders while singing as loud as it can!

9.description: Pussy willows in full catkin, soft grey furry buds all along the branches near water
9.childFriendlyNote: Willow branches are covered in soft grey puffs. Stroke them and they feel like the softest velvet

9.description: Robin flocks arriving in waves, singing dawn chorus even on cold mornings
9.childFriendlyNote: Flocks of orange-bellied robins are back! They sing so cheerfully it makes cold mornings feel warmer

9.description: First mountain bluebirds arriving from lower elevations, males an electric sky-blue hovering over grasslands
9.childFriendlyNote: A bird so blue it looks like a piece of sky! Mountain bluebirds hover like tiny helicopters over the grass

10.description: Mountain bluebirds returning to nesting areas, males hovering over open fields displaying brilliant blue plumage
10.childFriendlyNote: The bluest bird you've ever seen floats over the field like a bright blue leaf blown by the wind!

10.description: Robins everywhere now, singing from treetops and pulling worms from thawing lawns
10.childFriendlyNote: Robins tilt their heads sideways on the lawn. They're actually listening for worms wriggling underground!

10.description: Red-winged blackbirds in full song at every marsh and pond, females beginning to arrive
10.childFriendlyNote: Now the brown lady blackbirds arrive and the boys show off their red shoulders even harder!

10.description: Crocuses blooming in garden beds and along warm sidewalks, opening wide on sunny afternoons
10.childFriendlyNote: Crocuses open their cups wide to drink in the sunshine, then close up tight when clouds roll in!

10.description: Prairie dog towns fully active, animals kissing (touching teeth) to identify colony members
10.childFriendlyNote: Prairie dogs greet each other with a kiss! They touch their teeth together to say "you're one of us!"

10.description: Pussy willow catkins turning golden as they release pollen, first food for early bees
10.childFriendlyNote: The fuzzy silver puffs turn golden and dusty. Hungry bees visit them for the first meal of spring!

11.description: Pasque flowers, the first native wildflower, blooming on sunny hillsides, fuzzy purple cups often poking through remaining snow
11.childFriendlyNote: A fuzzy purple flower pushes right through the snow! Its stem is covered in soft silver hairs to keep it warm

11.description: Mountain bluebirds actively checking nest boxes and tree cavities, pairs forming
11.childFriendlyNote: Bluebird couples peek into nest boxes together: "Is this one good? What about that one over there?"

11.description: Western meadowlarks returning to grasslands, singing their beautiful bubbling flute-like song from fence posts
11.childFriendlyNote: A yellow-bellied bird on a fence post tips its head back and plays a flute, the most beautiful song in the West!

11.description: Robins beginning to build nests in sheltered spots, carrying mud and grass
11.childFriendlyNote: Watch a robin carry a beak-full of mud. It's making a perfect round bowl to hold its blue eggs!

11.description: Prairie dog towns bustling, animals grooming each other and standing sentinel on mounds
11.childFriendlyNote: One prairie dog always stands guard while the others eat. It barks loud if a hawk flies over!

12.description: Pasque flowers in peak bloom on foothills and open grasslands, furry stems and lavender petals
12.childFriendlyNote: Hillsides are dotted with fuzzy purple flowers. Each one has a golden sun of stamens in the middle!

12.description: Meadowlarks in full song, bright yellow breast with black V-necklace visible on fence posts
12.childFriendlyNote: The meadowlark wears a yellow shirt with a fancy black necklace and sings the prettiest song you ever heard!

12.description: Bluebird pairs established on territories, male perching conspicuously near nest cavities
12.childFriendlyNote: The bright blue dad bird sits right on top of the nest box like a shiny blue guard!

12.description: Garden daffodils blooming in town gardens and parks, cheerful yellow trumpets on sunny days
12.childFriendlyNote: Golden daffodils nod their trumpet-heads in the breeze like they're playing a sunny song!

12.description: Red-tailed hawk pairs building or refurbishing stick nests in cottonwoods and on cliff ledges
12.childFriendlyNote: A hawk carries a stick as big as your arm to its giant nest. It's redecorating for baby hawks!

12.description: First garter snakes emerging from winter dens on warm south-facing slopes, basking on rocks
12.childFriendlyNote: A stripy snake stretches out on a warm rock to soak up sunshine. It spent all winter sleeping underground!

13.description: First broad-tailed hummingbirds arriving at lower elevations, males making distinctive metallic wing trills in flight
13.childFriendlyNote: A tiny jewel-coloured bird zooms past making a cricket-like buzzing with its wings. It flew here from Mexico!

13.description: Pasque flowers developing feathery seed heads as blooms fade, silky plumes catching wind
13.childFriendlyNote: The purple flowers turn into fluffy feathery balls. Blow on them and tiny seeds float away like wishes!

13.description: Meadowlarks singing from every fence post and rise, the quintessential sound of the mountain grasslands
13.childFriendlyNote: Every fence post has its own singer. Meadowlarks fill the whole prairie with their bubbly flute song!

13.description: Ornamental cherries and crab apples beginning to bloom in town streets and parks, pink and white blossoms
13.childFriendlyNote: Town trees explode with pink flowers like nature's fireworks. Stand underneath and petals fall like confetti!

13.description: Prairie dogs actively mating, males chasing females around the colony with excited barking
13.childFriendlyNote: Prairie dog town is full of drama. They chase each other around and bark and bark and bark!

13.description: Canada geese returning to mountain lakes and parks, honking V-formations overhead, pairs claiming nest sites
13.childFriendlyNote: Look up when you hear honking! Geese fly in a V-shape. Each bird takes turns being the leader at the front

14.description: Crab apples and ornamental fruit trees in bloom across towns, clouds of pink and white blossoms
14.childFriendlyNote: Whole streets smell sweet! The crab apple trees look like big pink lollipops covered in buzzing bees

14.description: Broad-tailed hummingbirds arriving in greater numbers, wing trills audible before you see the bird
14.childFriendlyNote: You hear a strange buzzy trill and then (zip!) a tiny hummingbird rockets past your ear!

14.description: Meadowlarks nesting in grass tussocks, singing their complex flute-like melodies from fence posts
14.childFriendlyNote: The meadowlark's nest is hidden in the grass. The mama bird walks to it so sneakily no one can find it!

14.description: Mountain bluebirds nesting, female incubating while the sky-blue male guards nearby
14.childFriendlyNote: Mama bluebird sits on her eggs while papa bluebird keeps watch on the fence like a bright blue lookout!

14.description: Canada geese nesting on pond edges and islands, the gander aggressively guarding the sitting goose
14.childFriendlyNote: Don't get too close to a goose nest. The dad goose hisses and spreads his wings to say "Back off!"

15.description: Hummingbirds established at feeders and early-blooming flowers, males performing J-shaped dive displays
15.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird boy zooms up high then dives like a tiny roller coaster, making a loud buzz at the bottom!

15.description: Dandelions blooming across lawns and disturbed ground, providing crucial early nectar for bees
15.childFriendlyNote: Golden dandelion suns pop up everywhere. Bees love them because they're the first restaurant open for spring!

15.description: Meadowlarks on eggs in hidden grass nests, still singing powerfully from elevated perches
15.childFriendlyNote: The meadowlark sings its heart out from a fence post while its partner hides in the grass on the eggs!

15.description: Robins incubating their signature blue eggs, singing rich dawn chorus starting before sunrise
15.childFriendlyNote: Robin eggs are the most famous blue in nature: "robin's egg blue" is named after them!

15.description: Garter snakes fully active, hunting near streams and garden ponds for frogs and worms
15.childFriendlyNote: A stripy snake slithers through the grass by the stream. Its tongue flicks in and out to smell the world!

15.description: Lilac buds swelling in town gardens, leaves just beginning to unfurl on the bushes
15.childFriendlyNote: Fat purple buds on the lilac bush are about to burst open. Soon the whole garden will smell amazing!

16.description: Lilacs beginning to bloom in town gardens and along old homestead sites, heavy sweet fragrance
16.childFriendlyNote: Close your eyes near a lilac bush and breathe in. The smell is so sweet it feels like purple!

16.description: Hummingbirds nesting, the tiny female building a walnut-sized nest of spider silk and lichen on a branch
16.childFriendlyNote: The mama hummingbird's nest is as small as a walnut. She glues it together with spider webs!

16.description: Dandelion fields golden across lawns and meadows, first seed clocks forming
16.childFriendlyNote: Lawns turn gold with dandelions! Soon they'll become fluffy white puffballs perfect for wish-blowing

16.description: First goslings hatching, yellow fuzzy chicks following parents in a line to water
16.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow-green goslings waddle behind their parents in a line. Count how many babies in the family!

16.description: Cottonwood buds swelling and becoming sticky, releasing a sweet resinous fragrance called balm of Gilead
16.childFriendlyNote: Cottonwood buds are sticky with golden goo that smells like honey and medicine mixed together. Smell your fingers after touching one!

17.description: Lilacs in full bloom, heavy purple and white flower clusters perfuming entire neighbourhoods
17.childFriendlyNote: Lilac bushes are covered in purple and white flower clusters. Bury your nose in one and take a deep sniff!

17.description: Cottonwoods pushing out bright green leaves, the last major tree to leaf out along rivers and in towns
17.childFriendlyNote: Big cottonwood trees finally get their leaves! The new ones are bright shiny green and rattle in the breeze

17.description: Wild iris beginning to bloom in moist meadows and along ditches, elegant blue-purple flowers
17.childFriendlyNote: Wild iris flowers look like fancy purple butterflies landing in the wet meadow grass!

17.description: Pronghorn does moving to fawning areas in open grasslands, bucks in bachelor groups
17.childFriendlyNote: Pronghorn are the fastest animals in North America. They can run as fast as a car on the highway!

17.description: Barn swallows arriving from Central America, swooping and diving over fields and water catching insects
17.childFriendlyNote: Swooping, diving birds with forked tails are back from their winter holiday in Central America!

18.description: Chokecherry shrubs bursting into bloom, drooping clusters of small white flowers along streams and roadsides
18.childFriendlyNote: White flower clusters hang like tiny grape bunches on the chokecherry bush. Bees go crazy for them!

18.description: Cottonwoods in full new leaf, heart-shaped leaves rustling and flickering silver-green in the wind
18.childFriendlyNote: Cottonwood leaves are shaped like hearts and they shimmer and whisper in the wind. Listen to the tree talk!

18.description: Wild iris in full bloom in wet meadows, patches of blue-purple flowers swaying in the breeze
18.childFriendlyNote: Whole meadows turn purple with wild iris. Each flower has golden stripes inside to guide bees to the nectar!

18.description: Rattlesnakes emerging from winter dens and dispersing across grasslands, basking on warm rocks and trails
18.childFriendlyNote: Listen for a buzzy rattle sound near rocks. Rattlesnakes shake their tails to say "please don't step on me!"

18.description: Barn swallows building mud nests under eaves and bridges, swooping to collect mud from puddle edges
18.childFriendlyNote: Swallows carry tiny blobs of mud in their beaks to build a cup-shaped nest, one mud ball at a time!

18.description: Pronghorn does heavy with fawns, seeking isolated spots in the grasslands for birthing
18.childFriendlyNote: Mama pronghorn finds a quiet spot in the big grassy prairie. Her baby will be born soon and can run within days!

19.description: Blue columbine beginning to bloom at lower elevations, Colorado's state flower with elegant spurred petals
19.childFriendlyNote: Colorado's special flower looks like a blue and white star with long pointy tails, like a fairy's hat!

19.description: Chokecherry in full bloom, sweet almond-like fragrance drifting from white flower clusters
19.childFriendlyNote: Stand near a chokecherry bush and breathe deep. The white flowers smell like almonds and honey!

19.description: Prairie dog pups first appearing above ground, tiny and wobbly at burrow entrances
19.childFriendlyNote: Tiny baby prairie dogs peek out of their holes for the first time. They're so small and wiggly and curious!

19.description: Hummingbirds at peak activity visiting penstemons, columbines, and garden flowers
19.childFriendlyNote: Hummingbirds zip from flower to flower like tiny rockets. They visit hundreds of flowers every single day!

19.description: Barn swallows on eggs in mud nests, pairs swooping and chattering near barns and bridges
19.childFriendlyNote: Swallows chatter and swoop near their mud nests. Mama swallow is sitting on her eggs inside!

20.description: Columbines blooming in shaded mountain woods and along streams, delicate blue-and-white spurred flowers
20.childFriendlyNote: Each columbine has five blue petals with long nectar spurs. Only hummingbirds have tongues long enough to reach inside!

20.description: Indian paintbrush beginning to bloom at lower elevations, flame-red bracts brightening meadow edges
20.childFriendlyNote: It really does look like someone dipped a paintbrush in red paint and stuck it in the ground!

20.description: Cottonwood trees releasing fluffy white seeds, the "cotton" drifting through the air like summer snow
20.childFriendlyNote: It's snowing in May! Cottonwood trees send fluffy white puffs floating through the air. Catch one!

20.description: Pronghorn fawns being born, hiding motionless in the grass while mothers graze nearby
20.childFriendlyNote: Tiny pronghorn babies lie perfectly still in the grass. They have no scent so coyotes can't smell them!

20.description: Swallows swooping low over ponds and fields, catching insects on the wing with acrobatic turns
20.childFriendlyNote: Swallows are the best flyers in the bird world. They twist and turn and catch bugs right out of the air!

21.description: Indian paintbrush in bloom across foothill meadows, vibrant red-orange bracts among the grasses
21.childFriendlyNote: Fields are splashed with bright red paintbrush flowers, like an artist flung red paint across the meadow!

21.description: Columbines at peak in mountain forests and along trails, white inner petals and blue outer petals
21.childFriendlyNote: The columbine looks like a blue and white crown. It's so special it's against the law to pick it in Colorado!

21.description: Peak cottonwood fluff, white drifts accumulating against curbs and fences like midsummer snow
21.childFriendlyNote: Cottonwood fluff piles up like snow drifts! Each tiny puff carries a seed that could grow into a giant tree

21.description: Lupines blooming in mountain meadows and along roadsides, spires of blue-purple pea-like flowers
21.childFriendlyNote: Purple lupine towers stand like tiny Christmas trees decorated with blue-purple flowers!

21.description: Mule deer fawns being born, spotted brown babies hiding in tall grass and brush
21.childFriendlyNote: Baby deer have white spots like polka dots to help them hide in the dappled shade. If you see one, don't touch it!

22.description: Lupines in full bloom across mountain meadows, blue-purple spires mixed with other wildflowers
22.childFriendlyNote: Meadows are full of purple lupine towers buzzing with bees. Each flower is shaped like a tiny mouth!

22.description: Paintbrush at peak in foothill meadows, often growing alongside lupines in a red-and-blue display
22.childFriendlyNote: Red paintbrush and blue lupine grow side by side like nature's own Fourth of July decorations!

22.description: Hummingbirds feeding nestlings, females making constant trips between flowers and tiny nests
22.childFriendlyNote: Mama hummingbird feeds her babies by sticking her long beak into their mouths like a tiny sword, slurp!

22.description: Marmots sunning on rocks in mountain meadows, giving sharp whistle alarm calls when hikers approach
22.childFriendlyNote: Chubby marmots sunbathe on warm rocks and whistle loud when they see you. That's why they're called whistle pigs!

22.description: Aspens fully leafed out, round leaves trembling and flickering in the slightest breeze, groves bright green
22.childFriendlyNote: Aspen leaves dance and shimmer even when there's no wind. The flat stems make them tremble and whisper!

23.description: Larkspur blooming in mountain meadows and open woodlands, tall spikes of deep blue-purple flowers
23.childFriendlyNote: Tall blue larkspur spikes stand up in the meadow like purple candles. Each flower has a pointy spur on the back!

23.description: Paintbrush blooming at higher elevations now, joining the alpine wildflower display
23.childFriendlyNote: Higher and higher up the mountain, paintbrush flowers are popping open. The colour parade climbs uphill!

23.description: Marmots grazing on wildflowers and grasses, fattening up for their long hibernation
23.childFriendlyNote: Marmots stuff their cheeks with flowers and grass. They need to get as fat as possible before their winter sleep!

23.description: Pikas active in high-elevation talus fields, giving sharp "eek!" alarm calls from rock piles
23.childFriendlyNote: A tiny round animal that looks like a hamster with round ears goes "eek!" from between the rocks!

23.description: Afternoon thunderstorms building over the mountains, towering cumulus clouds and dramatic lightning displays
23.childFriendlyNote: Puffy white clouds grow into dark towers every afternoon, then boom! Thunder rumbles and rain smells amazing!

23.description: Hummingbirds visiting mountain wildflowers at peak, especially penstemons and scarlet gilia
23.childFriendlyNote: Hummingbirds love red flowers best. They zoom to every red thing, even red shirts and red hats!

24.description: Larkspur in full bloom across mountain meadows, deep blue spires swaying in afternoon breezes
24.childFriendlyNote: Blue larkspur flowers look like tiny birds perching on a tall green stick. Count how many flowers on one spike!

24.description: Lupines at peak in mountain meadows, some beginning to set seed pods that twist and pop in the sun
24.childFriendlyNote: Lupine seed pods twist and pop open in the hot sun. Listen for tiny snapping sounds on a warm afternoon!

24.description: Pikas beginning to gather flowers and grasses for hay piles, carrying mouthfuls back to their rock crevices
24.childFriendlyNote: The tiny pika carries a huge moustache of wildflowers back to its rock. It's making a hay pantry for winter!

24.description: Daily afternoon thunderstorms over the mountains, the smell of petrichor on dry earth after rain
24.childFriendlyNote: After the thunder booms and rain falls on dry ground, sniff the air. That amazing fresh smell is called petrichor!

24.description: Spotted mule deer fawns now following does, still wobbly on long legs in mountain meadows
24.childFriendlyNote: Baby deer trot behind their mamas on long wobbly legs. They still have their polka-dot camouflage coats!

25.description: Peak wildflower season in mountain meadows: paintbrush, lupine, columbine, larkspur, and asters creating a tapestry of colour
25.childFriendlyNote: Mountain meadows look like someone spilled every colour of paint: red, blue, purple, yellow, white, all mixed together!

25.description: Pikas in full haying mode, frantically gathering wildflowers and spreading them on rocks to dry
25.childFriendlyNote: Pikas spread flowers on sunny rocks to dry them. They're making tiny haystacks to eat all winter long!

25.description: Marmot pups emerging from burrows, playful young marmots wrestling and chasing near boulder fields
25.childFriendlyNote: Baby marmots play-fight and chase each other around the rocks like furry little kids at recess!

25.description: Hummingbirds at peak numbers in mountain wildflower meadows, constant buzz and chitter
25.childFriendlyNote: So many hummingbirds! They zoom past your ears making a cricket-trill sound with their wings

25.description: Afternoon monsoon storms building daily, dramatic lightning and heavy rain cooling mountain trails
25.childFriendlyNote: Every afternoon the mountains cook up a thunderstorm. Watch the clouds puff up like popcorn, then crack goes the lightning!

26.description: Paintbrush in full colour at higher elevations, reds and oranges mixed with alpine wildflowers
26.childFriendlyNote: Even way up high on the mountain, red paintbrush flowers glow like little campfires in the green grass!

26.description: Pikas continuing to gather hay, sharp alarm calls echoing across talus slopes when hawks pass
26.childFriendlyNote: The pika squeaks "eek!" and dives into the rocks when a hawk's shadow passes over, quick as lightning!

26.description: Aspen groves lush and green, leaves shimmering and rustling in summer breezes with a gentle rushing sound
26.childFriendlyNote: Stand in an aspen grove and close your eyes. Thousands of leaves whisper and shimmer like gentle rain!

26.description: Marmots basking on warm rocks, their sharp alarm whistles carrying across mountain valleys
26.childFriendlyNote: A marmot lies flat on a warm rock with its legs dangling. It looks like a furry pancake getting a suntan!

26.description: Barn swallow chicks growing in mud nests, parents swooping in constantly with beaks full of insects
26.childFriendlyNote: Baby swallows open their mouths so wide when a parent arrives. Four big yellow beaks pop out of the mud cup!

27.description: Fireweed beginning to bloom along roadsides and disturbed areas, tall magenta spikes opening from bottom to top
27.childFriendlyNote: Tall pink fireweed flowers open from the bottom up. When they reach the top, summer is almost over!

27.description: Intense afternoon monsoon storms, mushroom-shaped clouds building to 40,000 feet over the peaks
27.childFriendlyNote: Thunderclouds grow as tall as mountains in the afternoon sky. Count the seconds between flash and boom to see how far away!

27.description: Hummingbirds abundant in mountain gardens and wildflower meadows, juveniles now also visiting flowers
27.childFriendlyNote: Young hummingbirds are learning to fly! Watch them crash-land on flowers and figure out how to hover

27.description: Pikas working hard through peak flower season, drying haystacks growing on favourite rocks
27.childFriendlyNote: The pika's hay pile is getting big. It dries flowers in the sun and moves them inside before it rains!

27.description: Large yellow-and-black swallowtail butterflies nectaring on wildflowers and near streams
27.childFriendlyNote: A big yellow butterfly with black tiger stripes floats by. Its wings are as big as your hand!

28.description: Fireweed in full bloom along roads and clearings, vivid magenta spires half-open
28.childFriendlyNote: Fireweed spikes are halfway up with pink flowers. Summer is at its midpoint, just like the flowers!

28.description: Marmots visibly fattening, grazing heavily through mountain meadows in preparation for hibernation
28.childFriendlyNote: Marmots are getting so round! They eat and eat all summer so they have enough fat to sleep until spring

28.description: Aspen groves at their greenest, white bark standing out against deep green canopy and blue sky
28.childFriendlyNote: Aspen trunks are white as paper. People used to carve their names on them, but please don't, it hurts the tree!

28.description: Swallowtails puddling at damp spots on trails, groups gathering to sip minerals from mud
28.childFriendlyNote: Big yellow butterflies gather at mud puddles for a drink. They're having a butterfly pool party!

28.description: Barn swallow fledglings sitting on wires in a row, begging from parents who swoop past with insects
28.childFriendlyNote: Baby swallows line up on a wire like birds on a clothesline, begging for food with wide-open mouths!

29.description: Fireweed blooms climbing to the top of the stalk, a traditional signal that summer is waning
29.childFriendlyNote: Fireweed is almost to the top! Old-timers say when it blooms to the tip, frost is only six weeks away

29.description: Pikas harvesting intensely, large hay piles visible on rock ledges drying in the summer sun
29.childFriendlyNote: The pika's hay pile is huge now. It's been gathering all summer and its pantry is nearly full!

29.description: Hummingbirds feeding heavily on late-summer flowers, building fat reserves before migration
29.childFriendlyNote: Hummingbirds are eating extra-hard now. They need to get fat for their long flight back to Mexico!

29.description: Mule deer bucks in velvet, antlers nearly full-grown and covered in fuzzy brown skin
29.childFriendlyNote: Buck deer have fuzzy velvet on their antlers. It's like soft brown fabric covering the growing bone!

29.description: Monsoon thunderstorms continuing, spectacular double rainbows appearing over the mountains after storms
29.childFriendlyNote: After the storm, look east with the sun behind you. You might see a double rainbow arching over the mountains!

30.description: Fireweed blooming at the very top, lower seed pods splitting open to release fluffy white seeds
30.childFriendlyNote: Fireweed reached the top! The bottom pods burst open with fluffy white floss. Summer is almost done

30.description: Rabbitbrush beginning to show yellow buds in the dry foothills and along roadsides
30.childFriendlyNote: The grey-green rabbitbrush bushes are getting ready to explode into bright yellow flowers, not yet, but soon!

30.description: Mule deer bucks beginning to shed velvet from antlers, rubbing against trees to remove the drying skin
30.childFriendlyNote: Buck deer rub their antlers on trees to peel off the velvet. Sometimes you can see strips hanging like ribbons!

30.description: Second brood of swallowtails on the wing, worn first-brood adults and fresh new ones side by side
30.childFriendlyNote: Some swallowtails look tattered from a busy summer while brand-new ones are crisp and bright. Spot the difference!

30.description: Swallows raising second broods, parents and fledglings from first brood all hunting insects together
30.childFriendlyNote: The whole swallow family hunts together now, parents, big brothers and sisters, all swooping over the pond!

31.description: Rabbitbrush buds nearly open, grey-green bushes about to burst into golden bloom across the dry slopes
31.childFriendlyNote: Rabbitbrush is ready to pop. Any day now those grey bushes will be covered in bright golden flowers!

31.description: Elk bulls with hardened antlers, bachelor groups beginning to break up as rutting season approaches
31.childFriendlyNote: Big bull elk with huge antlers are getting grumpy. They'll soon be fighting over who gets to be the boss!

31.description: Hummingbird numbers beginning to thin as early migrants start heading south
31.childFriendlyNote: Some hummingbirds are already leaving! They're heading to Mexico, a journey as long as driving from Denver to Dallas

31.description: Nighthawks displaying at dusk, diving and making a booming sound with their wings, catching insects in flight
31.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, watch for birds with white wing patches diving through the sky, vroomm! Their wings make a cool boom sound!

31.description: Pikas making final hay-gathering runs, haystacks at their largest before being cached in rock crevices
31.childFriendlyNote: The pika's haystack is as big as a pillow, time to start tucking it into the rocks for winter!

32.description: Rabbitbrush bursting into bloom, turning hillsides and roadsides brilliant golden yellow
32.childFriendlyNote: The whole hillside turns gold! Rabbitbrush is the last big wildflower show before autumn starts

32.description: Nighthawk flocks gathering for migration, hundreds swooping over towns at dusk catching insects
32.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of nighthawks swoop together at sunset. They're having a farewell party before flying to South America!

32.description: Bucks with polished antlers, velvet fully shed, beginning to spar with other males
32.childFriendlyNote: Buck deer push their antlers together and wrestle. It sounds like clacking sticks in the woods!

32.description: Hummingbird numbers declining, rufous hummingbirds passing through on southbound migration
32.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbirds are leaving! Keep your feeders full. Tired travellers need a rest stop on their long journey

32.description: Prairie grasses turning golden and tawny, seed heads waving in warm August breezes
32.childFriendlyNote: The green grass is turning gold like a lion's mane. Run your hand through the seed heads and feel them tickle!

33.description: Rabbitbrush at peak bloom, attracting late-season butterflies and beetles, golden against dry grass
33.childFriendlyNote: Rabbitbrush is the last restaurant open for butterflies. They crowd around the golden flowers for one last meal!

33.description: Bull elk beginning early bugling, testing their voices in the cool mountain mornings
33.childFriendlyNote: Bull elk start practising their bugle call, a high-pitched scream that echoes off the mountain walls!

33.description: First hints of gold appearing in aspen leaves at the highest elevations, barely noticeable
33.childFriendlyNote: Way up on the mountain tops, a few aspen leaves are turning gold. Autumn is whispering "I'm coming!"

33.description: Prairie grasses fully golden, wild sunflowers and late asters blooming along roads and fields
33.childFriendlyNote: The prairies are a sea of gold. Stand in the middle and watch the grass waves ripple in the wind like water!

33.description: Red-tailed hawks and juvenile birds of the year soaring over golden grasslands, learning to hunt
33.childFriendlyNote: Young hawks are practising hunting. They swoop and miss a lot, but they're getting better every day!

34.description: Elk bugling increasing in mountain valleys, bulls beginning to gather cows into harems
34.childFriendlyNote: Elk bugling sounds like a haunted flute! The big bulls scream to say "this is my family, stay away!"

34.description: Aspen colour starting to turn at higher elevations, patches of gold appearing among the green
34.childFriendlyNote: Golden patches are spreading through the aspen forests. It's like someone spilled a paint bucket of gold!

34.description: Rabbitbrush still golden, the dominant colour along roadsides and open areas
34.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow rabbitbrush lines every road. It's like nature drew yellow racing stripes on the landscape!

34.description: First frost possible at higher elevations, ice crystals on grass and flowers in cold mountain mornings
34.childFriendlyNote: The first frost turns the meadow into a glittering diamond field. Every blade of grass wears an icy sparkle coat!

34.description: Nighthawk migration in full swing, large flocks moving southward in the late afternoon sky
34.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of nighthawks stream across the sky heading south. Wave goodbye until next summer!

35.description: Elk rut intensifying, bulls bugling constantly at dawn and dusk, the defining sound of mountain autumn
35.childFriendlyNote: Elk bugles echo through the valleys at sunrise. It's one of the wildest sounds in all of nature!

35.description: Aspen colour spreading rapidly downslope, mountainsides becoming a patchwork of gold, orange, and green
35.childFriendlyNote: Whole mountainsides are turning gold! The aspens look like rivers of liquid gold running down the slopes

35.description: Last broad-tailed hummingbirds departing, a few stragglers fuelling up at feeders and late flowers
35.childFriendlyNote: The last hummingbirds are tanking up at the feeder like tiny airplanes getting fuel before a long flight!

35.description: Rabbitbrush flowers fading to dusty gold, seed heads forming
35.childFriendlyNote: The rabbitbrush flowers are getting fuzzy and dusty. They're turning into fluffy seed puffs

35.description: Mule deer bucks with polished antlers, necks thickening for the coming rut
35.childFriendlyNote: Buck deer look extra tough right now. Their necks are thick and muscly and their antlers shine in the sun!

36.description: Peak elk rut, bulls bugling, sparring, and herding cows, one of the great wildlife spectacles of North America
36.childFriendlyNote: Giant bull elk crash their antlers together with a clack!. They're wrestling to see who's the strongest

36.description: Aspen gold at or near peak, entire mountainsides blazing yellow and orange, the famous Rocky Mountain autumn
36.childFriendlyNote: The mountains are on fire with colour, but it's not real fire, it's millions of golden aspen leaves!

36.description: Magpies in large autumn flocks, their black-and-white plumage striking against golden aspens
36.childFriendlyNote: Big flocks of chattering magpies fly between the golden trees, black and white against yellow and blue!

36.description: Hard frosts common now, blackening garden plants and coating everything in thick white crystals at dawn
36.childFriendlyNote: Frost so thick it looks like snow! Touch a frozen leaf and it crumbles into glittery pieces

36.description: Dark-eyed juncos arriving from higher elevations and the north, flocks building at feeders
36.childFriendlyNote: Little grey "snowbirds" are back at the feeder. They come down from the mountains when it gets cold up there!

37.description: Peak aspen colour at mid-elevations, leaves beginning to fall at the highest spots, golden carpet on trails
37.childFriendlyNote: Walk through the aspen grove and golden leaves rain down like coins. Scuffle through the golden carpet!

37.description: Elk rut continuing, bulls exhausted from constant bugling and fighting, ribs starting to show
37.childFriendlyNote: The bull elk haven't eaten in weeks because they're too busy fighting. They look tired but still bugle at dawn!

37.description: Mule deer rut beginning, bucks chasing does across hillsides and through aspen groves
37.childFriendlyNote: Deer are chasing each other through the golden aspens. Buck deer are showing off for the lady deer!

37.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring over golden grasslands, migrant hawks joining resident birds
37.childFriendlyNote: More hawks than usual circle in the sky. Local hawks are joined by travellers passing through!

37.description: Canada geese in migration formation, noisy V-shaped flocks honking overhead
37.childFriendlyNote: Look up when you hear honking. Big V's of geese are heading south, trading leaders so nobody gets too tired!

38.description: Aspen colour fading at higher elevations, peak colour moving to mid and lower elevations now
38.childFriendlyNote: The golden wave moves downhill. Up high the aspens are bare, but down low they're still blazing gold!

38.description: Elk rut winding down, exhausted bulls beginning to separate from cow herds
38.childFriendlyNote: The elk battles are winding down. The tired bull elk wander off to rest and eat after weeks of fighting

38.description: Mule deer rut in full swing, bucks sparring and chasing does, visible in open areas at dawn and dusk
38.childFriendlyNote: Deer bucks crash their antlers together in the misty morning. It sounds like a stick fight in the woods!

38.description: Junco flocks growing, winter populations settling in at feeders and in shrubby areas
38.childFriendlyNote: More and more grey juncos arrive every day. They've come down from the mountains for the winter!

38.description: Cottonwoods turning bright yellow along rivers and in town, large heart-shaped leaves falling
38.childFriendlyNote: Big yellow cottonwood leaves shaped like hearts spin and twirl as they fall. Catch one for good luck!

39.description: Aspens past peak at most elevations, bare branches showing at the top, last gold clinging lower down
39.childFriendlyNote: The aspen show is almost over. Bare white trunks stand like skeletons at the top while gold still glows below

39.description: Mule deer rut continuing, bucks visibly thinner from constant chasing and sparring
39.childFriendlyNote: The buck deer look skinny. They haven't been eating because they've been too busy showing off!

39.description: Cottonwoods shedding golden leaves, rivers of yellow flowing along waterways against brown grasslands
39.childFriendlyNote: Golden cottonwood leaves pile up on the ground and float down the stream, a golden river under a golden tree!

39.description: Large flocks of geese staging on ponds and reservoirs, resting before continuing south
39.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of geese rest on the lake like a noisy parking lot. They honk and splash and argue all day!

39.description: First snow dusting the highest peaks, a dramatic white cap above the gold and brown of the valleys
39.childFriendlyNote: The mountain tops get their first white snow cap. They look like they're wearing fluffy white hats!

40.description: First snow possible in valley towns, often melting by midday but signalling winter's approach
40.childFriendlyNote: The first snow in town! It might melt by lunchtime, but those first flakes on your tongue taste like winter!

40.description: Elk herds beginning to move toward winter range, bulls rejoining small groups
40.childFriendlyNote: Elk families start walking downhill to warmer valleys. It's like their own autumn road trip!

40.description: Mule deer beginning autumn migration from high summer range to lower winter areas
40.childFriendlyNote: Deer are moving downhill to town. You might see more deer in your neighbourhood as winter approaches!

40.description: Magpies in autumn flocks, conspicuous in bare trees, caching food for winter
40.childFriendlyNote: Magpies are hiding food everywhere: under leaves, in gutters, in fence holes. Will they remember all the spots?

40.description: Junco winter flocks established, hopping on the ground under feeders and bushes
40.childFriendlyNote: Juncos hop around under the bird feeder cleaning up spilled seeds. They're the clean-up crew!

41.description: Elk migration in full swing, large herds visible moving through valleys and across roads
41.childFriendlyNote: Huge herds of elk march through the valleys. Sometimes they walk right across the road and you have to wait!

41.description: Mule deer migration continuing, more deer appearing in towns and lower foothills
41.childFriendlyNote: Deer are everywhere! They walk through yards, munch on bushes, and stare at you with their big brown eyes

41.description: Aspens mostly bare, white trunks with dark eye-shaped scars standing stark against grey and blue skies
41.childFriendlyNote: Bare white aspen trunks have dark eye-shaped marks. A whole grove looks like it's watching you with hundreds of eyes!

41.description: Magpie flocks noisy and bold, their empty domed nests visible in bare trees
41.childFriendlyNote: Now you can see magpie nests in the bare trees, big messy stick domes that look like bird castles!

41.description: Mountain chickadees moving to lower elevations, joining mixed flocks with juncos and nuthatches
41.childFriendlyNote: Mountain chickadees look like regular chickadees with a white racing stripe over their eye, "chick-a-dee-dee!"

42.description: Mule deer settling into winter range in towns and lower foothills, bucks beginning to shed antlers
42.childFriendlyNote: Deer are dropping their antlers again. The yearly cycle starts over! Search the hillsides for treasures

42.description: Junco flocks fully established for winter, trilling songs and flashing white tail feathers
42.childFriendlyNote: Juncos are here for the whole winter. They'll be your little grey feeder friends until spring!

42.description: Elk herds on winter range, large groups visible in valley meadows and on feed grounds
42.childFriendlyNote: Huge groups of elk gather in the snowy valleys, sometimes hundreds all together!

42.description: Snow draped on ponderosa pine and Douglas fir branches, green boughs bent under white weight
42.childFriendlyNote: Pine trees wear snow like white frosting on green cake. Brush a branch and whoosh, a mini snowstorm!

42.description: Red-tailed hawks perched on bare cottonwoods and poles, easily visible against grey October skies
42.childFriendlyNote: Hawks are easy to spot now that leaves are gone. Big puffed-up birds sit on bare branches watching everything!

43.description: Magpies conspicuous in bare trees and on snowy ground, iridescent feathers flashing in thin autumn sun
43.childFriendlyNote: Magpie feathers aren't just black. Look close in the sun and you'll see green, blue, and purple shimmer!

43.description: Junco flocks busy at feeders, their grey-and-white plumage blending with the November landscape
43.childFriendlyNote: Juncos match the grey sky and white snow perfectly. They're wearing winter camouflage!

43.description: Mule deer in winter coats, thick grey-brown fur keeping them warm in freezing temperatures
43.childFriendlyNote: Deer put on their fluffy winter coats. Their fur is hollow, so it traps warm air like a sleeping bag!

43.description: Steller's jays moving to lower elevations, visiting feeders and caching pinyon pine nuts
43.childFriendlyNote: Steller's jays swoop in from the mountains. They scream and grab seeds and fly off to hide them!

43.description: Coyotes in thick winter coats, howling at dusk, more visible as vegetation dies back
43.childFriendlyNote: Coyotes look extra fluffy in their winter fur. Listen at sunset for their howling song across the cold air!

44.description: Elk settled on winter range, herds grazing in valley meadows, bulls shedding antlers
44.childFriendlyNote: Big elk herds stand in the snowy fields. The boys are starting to lose their antlers one by one!

44.description: Magpies feeding on anything they can find, from roadkill to bird feeders, chattering loudly
44.childFriendlyNote: Magpies eat just about anything. They're nature's cleanup crew with the fanciest outfits!

44.description: Ponderosa pines vivid green against fresh snow, the warm orange bark striking in low autumn light
44.childFriendlyNote: Ponderosa pines are the toughest trees, green and strong while everything else is bare and brown!

44.description: Red-tails hunting along roads, perched on poles watching for voles in stubble fields
44.childFriendlyNote: Hawks sit on every other telephone pole along country roads. They're watching for mice like nature's security cameras!

44.description: First good tracking snow reveals rabbit, squirrel, deer, and coyote trails through neighbourhoods
44.childFriendlyNote: Fresh snow is like a detective's notebook. Every animal that walked by left footprints for you to read!

45.description: Juncos in full winter abundance, large flocks scratching under feeders and along hedge lines
45.childFriendlyNote: Juncos are everywhere! Count how many you can see under the bird feeder. Sometimes there are dozens!

45.description: Great horned owls beginning courtship hooting, deep duets echoing in the cold November night
45.childFriendlyNote: Owls start their love songs early! Listen at bedtime for "hoo-hoo-hooooo hoo-hoo" from the big trees

45.description: Mule deer in winter groups, browsing on sagebrush and whatever green they can find
45.childFriendlyNote: Deer munch on sagebrush. It's not very tasty but it's green when everything else is brown and dead!

45.description: Coyotes more visible in early dusk, trotting through open areas with thick winter coats
45.childFriendlyNote: A fluffy coyote trots across the snowy field at sunset. It looks like a wild dog on a mission!

45.description: Steller's jays noisy at feeders, their bold blue colour vivid against grey and white landscape
45.childFriendlyNote: The Steller's jay is the loudest bird at the feeder. It screams "shack shack shack" and scares everyone else away!

46.description: Magpies in winter flocks, long tails streaming behind them in flight against snowy backgrounds
46.childFriendlyNote: Magpies fly with their super-long tails streaming behind them like black-and-white kites!

46.description: Great horned owl pairs hooting in courtship, choosing nest sites in cottonwoods and on cliff ledges
46.childFriendlyNote: Two owls hoot back and forth to each other in the dark: the deep one is dad, the higher one is mum!

46.description: Elk in large winter herds, pawing through snow for grass, steam rising from their breath in cold air
46.childFriendlyNote: Elk breathe out clouds of steam in the cold. A whole herd makes a misty fog as they eat!

46.description: Juncos and other sparrows sheltering in dense bushes, huddled together for warmth on cold nights
46.childFriendlyNote: At bedtime, juncos squeeze together in thick bushes to share body heat, a feathery sleep-over!

46.description: Ponderosa and Douglas fir provide the only green in the landscape, sheltering birds from winter winds
46.childFriendlyNote: Evergreen trees are the heroes of winter. They stay green and give birds and squirrels a place to hide from storms!

47.description: Fresh snow reveals overnight visitors: rabbit, deer, coyote, and fox tracks crisscrossing yards and fields
47.childFriendlyNote: Check the snow first thing in the morning. You can tell exactly who visited your yard while you were sleeping!

47.description: Red-tailed hawks puffed up on perches, conserving energy in the cold, hunting during brief warm spells
47.childFriendlyNote: The hawk fluffs up its feathers like a puffy jacket to stay warm. It looks twice as big as in summer!

47.description: Magpies foraging in small groups, their chattering calls breaking the winter silence
47.childFriendlyNote: Magpies chatter and gossip all day long. They seem to have so much to say to each other!

47.description: Mule deer gathering in sheltered valleys and on south-facing slopes where snow melts first
47.childFriendlyNote: Deer huddle on sunny hillsides where the snow melts. They're smart about finding the warmest spots!

47.description: Great horned owls hooting loudly in early evening, establishing territories for nesting season
47.childFriendlyNote: The great horned owl hoots as soon as it gets dark. Listen right after sunset for that deep "who-who-who"

48.description: Ponderosa pine and Douglas fir standing green against fresh snow, the backbone of the winter landscape
48.childFriendlyNote: Green pines look like Christmas trees covered in snow frosting. Sniff the bark for that cookie smell!

48.description: Juncos feeding actively in the short winter days, needing to find enough calories before the long cold night
48.childFriendlyNote: Juncos eat fast because winter days are short. They need a full tummy to survive the long cold night!

48.description: Great horned owls may begin nesting in late November, sitting on eggs through December snowstorms
48.childFriendlyNote: Some owls are already sitting on eggs! They nest in winter because their babies need lots of time to grow

48.description: Steller's jays retrieving cached seeds from hiding spots, their memory remarkable
48.childFriendlyNote: The Steller's jay remembers where it buried hundreds of seeds. It finds them even under the snow!

48.description: Coyotes yipping and howling at dusk, sound carrying far in the crisp cold air
48.childFriendlyNote: Coyote howls sound extra loud and spooky in the cold night air. The sound bounces off everything!

49.description: Elk in deep winter mode, large herds concentrated on sheltered winter ranges, some still carrying antlers
49.childFriendlyNote: Elk stand shoulder to shoulder in the snow. They share body heat to stay warm in the freezing cold

49.description: Magpies bold and adaptable in winter, following deer and elk herds to scavenge
49.childFriendlyNote: Clever magpies follow the elk around. They pick bugs off the elk's back and the elk don't even mind!

49.description: Orion and winter constellations brilliant in the dry mountain air, the Milky Way visible from dark locations
49.childFriendlyNote: The dry mountain air makes stars extra sparkly. Find Orion the Hunter and his three-star belt in the south!

49.description: Red-tailed hawks on fence posts and poles, hunting the few daylight hours for rodents
49.childFriendlyNote: Hawks have to catch enough mice in just a few hours of daylight. Every minute of winter sunshine counts!

49.description: Ponderosa pines dusted with snow, orange bark glowing in low winter sun, butterscotch scent on warm afternoons
49.childFriendlyNote: Even in December, a sunny afternoon warms the ponderosa bark enough to release that amazing cookie smell!

50.description: Great horned owls on nests or preparing to nest, deep hooting duets audible on cold clear nights
50.childFriendlyNote: Owls are nesting in December! Mama owl keeps her eggs warm even when it's below zero outside, amazing!

50.description: Mule deer in heavy winter coats, gathered in sheltered canyons and town edges, browsing sagebrush
50.childFriendlyNote: Deer wear their thickest winter coats. Hollow fur traps air like a puffy jacket to keep them warm!

50.description: Magpies roosting communally in dense trees at night, dispersing in noisy groups at first light
50.childFriendlyNote: Magpies sleep together in the same tree every night. In the morning they all fly out chattering at once!

50.description: Snow tracking at its best: mouse tunnels, rabbit hops, deer trails, and coyote paths visible after fresh snow
50.childFriendlyNote: Snow is nature's story book. Mouse trails look like tiny zippers, and you can follow them to see where they went!

50.description: Juncos foraging busily on short winter days, flocking around feeders and hedgerows
50.childFriendlyNote: Juncos eat all day long in winter. They need to fill up before the long, cold, 15-hour night!

51.description: Ponderosa pine and Douglas fir standing strong in winter, green boughs heavy with fresh snow
51.childFriendlyNote: The tallest ponderosas wear snow on their branches like white sleeves. They've been standing here for hundreds of years!

51.description: Great horned owls incubating through the shortest days, calling at dusk from snow-covered perches
51.childFriendlyNote: The owl sits on her eggs through blizzards and freezing nights. She's the bravest bird in the forest!

51.description: Elk herds on winter range, surviving on dry grass and browse, calves nearly full-grown
51.childFriendlyNote: The elk calves born last spring are almost as big as their mums now. They grew so fast!

51.description: Steller's jays bright blue against the snow, raiding feeders and screaming from the pines
51.childFriendlyNote: The bold blue jay lands right on the feeder pole and screams. It wants all the seeds for itself!

51.description: The longest night of the year: Orion, Sirius, and the winter constellations blaze in crystal-clear mountain air
51.childFriendlyNote: The longest night has the most stars! Find the brightest star in the sky. That's Sirius, the dog star, following Orion!

52.description: Mule deer in winter survival mode, conserving energy, moving little, browsing on sagebrush and juniper
52.childFriendlyNote: Deer move slowly to save energy in the deep cold. Every calorie counts when food is hard to find!

52.description: Magpies bold and noisy as ever, black-and-white plumage crisp against the holiday snow
52.childFriendlyNote: Magpies are dressed in black and white like they're going to a fancy party, and they never stop chatting!

52.description: Coyotes hunting in the cold, pouncing through snow to catch mice, their yipping chorus echoing at dusk
52.childFriendlyNote: Coyotes leap high and dive nose-first into the snow. They heard a mouse underneath and pounce!

52.description: Ponderosa pine fragrant even in deep winter, warm bark a beacon of life in the frozen landscape
52.childFriendlyNote: Even in the coldest week of the year, hug a ponderosa on a sunny day and breathe in, warm vanilla magic!

52.description: Great horned owls hooting through the longest nights, the deep call a signature sound of the mountain winter
52.childFriendlyNote: As the year ends, the owl's deep hoot echoes through the cold mountains. Goodnight, wild world!
